P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Dollar accounts are standard retail products in Peru. BCP's Cuenta en Dólares can be opened with no minimum amount, earns interest in dollars, and lets you exchange dollars and soles in its app or website (BCP). BCP's terms limit personal savings accounts to personal and family use and may close accounts used for business-type flows (news report, not captured), so use a business account if you invoice heavily.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Independent workers earning 'cuarta categoría' (professional or independent-service) income must register in the RUC with SUNAT. With a DNI you can do it online, through the SUNAT 'App Personas' (Play Store or App Store) or the SUNAT portal. With another document (carné de extranjería, or a passport with a visa that allows income-generating activities), you register in person at any Centro de Servicios al Contribuyente. You must register and validate an email address and mobile number (already-registered taxpayers had until 31 August 2026). Fee: not stated by SUNAT.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Nuevo RUS (NRUS) for small businesses pays a fixed monthly quota instead of income tax and IGV. Category 1 covers income or purchases up to S/ 5,000 a month (quota S/ 20); Category 2 covers more than S/ 5,000 up to S/ 8,000 (quota S/ 50). A 'Categoría Especial' for natural persons who meet its conditions requires no monthly payment (SUNAT). TRAP for freelancers: NRUS is for business ('con negocio', third-category) income. Independent professional services are taxed as fourth-category income with electronic receipts for fees (see L1). Guides say some liberal professions cannot use NRUS (not confirmed on SUNAT). Above S/ 96,000 a year, taxpayers move to RER or RMT (search summary).

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: National identity card: National Identity Card (Peru) (Wikipedia, compulsory-ID list). National Document of Identification or Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI). Banks and payment platforms usually also accept a passport; their exact lists were not captured. Under Law 26497 the DNI, issued by RENIEC, is compulsory for all nationals and is the only personal identity card for civil, commercial, administrative and judicial acts (Congress of Peru).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
